notes:
Inbound via self-serve signup Feb 25. Product team building in-app assistant for their CRM product. They stressed streaming/low-latency — target p50 ~120–180ms and p95 <600ms for snappy UX. Small engineering team (2 backend, 1 mobile, 1 frontend) — want fastest time-to-value. Mentioned they prefer hosted API to avoid infra ops.

Security: SMB but servicing enterprise customers; requests SOC2 report and SSO support. Cost-sensitive: want to use smaller quantized models or Redwood routing to reduce token spend.

Pricing: asked about burst capacity and whether dedicated reserved options exist later. Wants clear per-token estimate at 100 req/s peak.

Tone: pragmatic, fast-moving. Quote from call: "We need that streaming feel; customers drop off if responses lag."

use_case_summary: HaloQuarry is a B2B SaaS CRM that will embed a streaming in-app assistant for quick, contextual help and task automation. Primary goals: low latency streaming, deterministic streaming tokens (partial responses), low cold-start for first token. They expect 50–150 concurrent users during early launch, with burst to ~300 concurrent. Preferred model family: small/efficient open models or Redwood curated low-latency variants. Wants route fallback to cheaper model when under heavy load.
additional_context: POC scope: 2-week integration with hosted API streaming, basic analytics, and cost/latency dashboard. Customer ready to pay for early POC if SOC2 evidence provided. Engineering timeline: ship Beta in 8–10 weeks after successful POC.
